chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

He said to me: 'Pray in the night of the 21st and the night of the 23rd of the month of Ramadan; in each of them, if you are able, one hundred rak'ahs, in addition to the thirteen [nightly prayers], and stay awake in them until morning, for it is recommended that you be in prayer, supplication, and humility, for it is hoped that the Night of Decree is in one of them.'
And [it is mentioned that] 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.'

I said to him: 'How is it better than a thousand months?' He said: 'The worship in it is better than the worship in a thousand months, and the Night of Decree is not in those months, but it occurs in the month of Ramadan.'
And 'In it is made distinct every precise matter.'
I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'Whatever occurs during the year is written in it, and the delegation [of angels/decree] to Mecca is written in it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and virtues of the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs Samaanah to perform 100 rak'ahs of night prayer on the 21st and 23rd of Ramadan, emphasizing prolonged devotion to capture the Night of Decree. The Imam clarifies that the virtue lies in the quality of worship during these specific nights, which are distinct from other months as they serve as the time when annual decrees (*al-wafd*) are finalized and dispatched. This underscores the Shia emphasis on active spiritual preparation and the belief that divine destiny is determined during these pivotal nights of Ramadan.
